signoff: Second opinion only. This report does NOT confer Antigravity mathematical sign-off, and nothing in it is a proof of the underlying fairness claims. Every verdict below is a reading of the cited read-only authority plus a check against the current tree, with the numeric toys I ran listed under 'tests'.
summary: Independent read-only review of C0's seven escalations. Verdicts: E1 partially supported (accept the whole-district reduction as a definition, but C0 understates that an agent-independent band filter makes FEFx identical to EFX on any band-compliant delivered map, so no existence guarantee transfers from barman2023gac); E2 supported (universal/EFX quantifier is correct, MATH_REVIEW 4.4's existential form is wrong) with three defects in C0's own text; E3 supported (no rep home coordinate exists anywhere in the tree, drivability is unimplementable); E4 supported on reject-by-default but C0's proposed clip mechanism is unsound and I give a verified 2x2 counterexample in which the eps_floor clip makes the Hungarian solve pick a bargaining-infeasible matching while a fully feasible one exists, producing a false reject; E5 supported (strict convexity of a fixed cost matrix is a category error) with four named replacement properties and one correction C0 missed, namely that plan invariant 5 (scale invariance) is broken by an absolute reservation vector and restored only because compute_reservation_vector is positively homogeneous of degree 1; E6 is governance not mathematics and the collision is wider than C0 states, since docs/units/U14-fullprob.md also owns td/stage2_state.py, tools/full_plan.py and both R1/R2 test files; E7 supported and stronger than C0 claims, since uniform mode at d_i = d_floor is provably clip-free and never rejects for any gamma in [0,1). I also found four defects in C0 outside E1-E7: a self-contradictory zero-valued-zip paragraph, a regression anchor in section 12 that is not reproducible from the declared API, an incomplete scale-invariance qualification in section 5, and a section 9 matching vehicle (channel.match on clipped centered gains) that conflicts with both channel.match's own positivity raise and the mask machinery the file already contains.

escalations.question: Is the whole-district filter A_j in F_i a faithful reduction of barman2023gac's FEF over feasible subsets?
escalations.c0_supported: Yes for the reduction itself. Auditing a delivered allocation only ever compares rep i against the bundle rep j actually holds, so 'test A_j in F_i once, then compare' is the correct instantiation of a feasible-envy axiom on a delivered map. It must be written as a definition of this audit, never as a theorem inherited from the paper, and C0 already says that.
what_c0_understates: barman2023gac's feasibility is agent-specific: LIT_economic-theory.md:228-231 says 'subsets the envying agent could actually have received, given agent-specific sizes and budgets'. C0's filter is agent-independent by construction (contract section 1: F[i,j] = band_ok[j] for every i, because the model has no per-rep capacity). The capacity band and contiguity are properties of the bundle, not of the agent.

Consequence: on a band-compliant delivered map every pair is applicable, so the contracted FEFx verdict is numerically identical to a plain EFX verdict. The feasibility filter can only fire on districts that violate their own band.

Consequence for existence: with F_i agent-independent and containing every delivered bundle, FEFx reduces to EFX, and EFX existence is open in general for n >= 4. The only positive result in the repository's own authority is chaudhury2021 (LIT_economic-theory.md:215-223): an EFX allocation exists with fewer than n goods left unallocated, i.e. it needs a charity set. A delivered map is complete and has no charity set. So a FEFx failure on the delivered map is the expected outcome, not a surprise, and plan DoD item 4 ('zero feasible envy') should be recorded as likely unattainable rather than merely unguaranteed.

Consequence for DOMAIN_economic-theory.md N1 (line 759): its 'overturns if' condition is 'a wide EF1 failure that is not an FEFx failure'. EFX is strictly stronger than EF1 (contract section 1, correct), so FEFx passes are a subset of EF1 passes; the only way N1's condition can arise is through the filter excluding a pair. Under an agent-independent band filter that requires a band-violating delivered district. N1's diagnostic is therefore unreachable unless an agent-specific F_i is adopted (see E3).
escalations.recommendation: Adopt the whole-district reduction, stated as this audit's definition. Add three requirements: (1) the audit reports n_applicable, n_infeasible_districts and the band-violation mass per infeasible district, so a reader can see whether the filter did any work at all; (2) the contract and any downstream note are forbidden from citing barman2023gac as evidence that FEFx will hold on the delivered map, and cite chaudhury2021 for the charity-set gap instead; (3) Antigravity is asked explicitly whether it wants an agent-specific F_i, because that single choice decides whether N1's diagnostic is reachable (E3).
escalations.hazard: Band infeasibility is a map defect signal, not an agent property. Level 2 admits band slack of 0.02 * tau (tools/plan_realise.py:115 BAND_SLACK, :1284 slack_b = band_slack * 0.5 * (L+U)), and level 0 records a per-slot band_hi that already includes the state-cap allowance a_s (tools/full_plan.py:518-547). So the districts the filter excludes are exactly the ones the repair pushed out of band, and excluding them excuses all envy against the worst-drawn districts. If infeasible_for_agent pairs are folded silently into a not-applicable total, the audit becomes weakest precisely where the map is most suspect. Mirror those districts into the capacity report as violations, and never let 'not applicable' absorb them without the mass being printed.

escalations.question: MATH_REVIEW.md 4.4 writes the existential (EF1) removal quantifier under the name FEFx; adopt the EFx universal reading?
escalations.c0_supported: Yes. The 'x' suffix in this literature is the universal removal quantifier, and chaudhury2021's charity-set result (LIT_economic-theory.md:218-219) is an EFX result, which is the universal form. MATH_REVIEW.md:107 writing 'exists z in V_j' under the heading FEFx is internally inconsistent, exactly as C0 finding 6 says. The closed forms are right: universal removal reduces to subtracting min_z u_i(z), existential to max_z u_i(z), by additivity. C0's toys (a) and (b) in contract section 13 reproduce on my check.
defects_in_c0: Contract section 1 'Zero-valued zips' contradicts itself. It asserts 'min_z u_i(z) = 0 whenever i holds no book in A_j' and then asserts 'BOT = common_min >= 0'. Under C0's own chosen valuation (td/channel.py:278-281, common_z = c2*T_z + c_free*S_free_z + lam*M_z added for every rep including non-holders) a non-holder contributes common_z, which is strictly positive on any zip with nonzero T, S_free or M. So min is common_min > 0, not 0. The first clause is only true under the masked convention (td/model.py:139-143 zeroes non-candidates). Delete the first clause or bind it to the convention.

Textbook EFX restricts the universal quantifier to items with u_i(z) > 0, because otherwise a zero-valued item turns EFX into plain EF. C0's uniform min over all z is therefore STRICTER than textbook EFX whenever a zero-valued zip is present, not equal to it. Verified toy: u_i(A_i) = 4, items [7, 0]; uniform-min residual is 7 (fail), textbook nonzero-only residual is 0 (pass), plain EF residual is 7 (fail). Under the gain_matrix convention this case is essentially empty; under the masked convention it is common. C0's 'no zip is skipped for being zero-valued' is a defensible conservative choice but must not be labelled plain 'EFX' without that qualification, and the audit should count pairs where min_z u_i(z) == 0.

Contract section 12's regression anchor is not reproducible from the section 9 API. td/model.py::fairness (lines 310-345) consumes the MASKED utility matrix from model.utilities, uses n = U.shape[0] (every rep in reps_order, including unmatched ones whose g_i is 0) as the proportionality divisor, compares with a 1e-12 additive slack, and returns four keys: ef1, n_ef1_failures, envy_over_umax, prop_shortfall, where prop_shortfall is a NORMALIZED non-negative quantity max_i max(0, u_i(Z)/n - g_i)/max_z u_i(z). The contract's compute_envy_matrix declares prop_gap / prop_gap_min (signed, raw nats, the form DOMAIN_economic-theory.md:488 reports as -12.0248), declares n = |R_selected|, and declares no envy_over_umax or prop_shortfall. Three of those four differences break the pinned equality.

Contract section 9 routes the centered match through 'channel.match-equivalent on centered'. channel.match raises on any non-positive entry (td/channel.py:298-300), and with a reservation the raw centered surplus g - d_i is negative on many edges (my toy check: 5 of 9 edges at alpha=0.814, gamma=0.60). It only avoids the raise because of the clip, which makes the clip load-bearing for feasibility rather than a numerical guard as section 3 claims.
escalations.recommendation: Adopt the universal (EFX) reading and correct MATH_REVIEW.md:107. Then: (1) add a valuation switch to the audit API, valuation in {'masked','gain_matrix'}, defaulting to 'gain_matrix' for the FEFx verdict, and pin the section 12 anchor test at valuation='masked', n = U.shape[0], slack 1e-12, returning all four fairness() keys unchanged alongside the new signed prop_gap_min; (2) state in the contract that the uniform-min form equals textbook EFX whenever every zip has positive value to the envier, which gain_matrix guarantees except on all-zero zips, and emit a zero_valued_zip_pairs count; (3) keep C0's timing rule, which is correct and is the only non-vacuous option, and record why: re-testing the band after removal drops M(A_j) below L for essentially every zip, so a post-removal feasibility test would mark nearly every pair not-applicable and the audit would return nothing.
escalations.hazard: The two valuation conventions can give different EF1 verdicts on the same delivered map, because the mask zeroes a non-candidate's ambient term c2*T_z + c_free*S_free_z + lam*M_z. Any comparison of 'plain EF1 before vs after' that silently switches convention is meaningless. Every emitted verdict must carry the convention name, and the audit must not recompute utilities its own way: reuse channel.gain_matrix and model.utilities, do not reimplement either.

escalations.question: Does geographic (drivability) feasibility belong in F_i at all, given no rep-home data exists?
escalations.c0_supported: Yes, and I verified the data claim independently. The only coordinates in the tree are ZCTA internal points per zip (td/geo.py:147-166) and district-level geometry; state_borders.home(j) is the state holding the plurality of a district's mass (td/solvers/state_borders.py:33-57), which is a property of the district, not of a rep. CellTable.reps is derived purely from who holds book (td/channels.py:360). There is no rep home ZIP, no rep centroid, and no rep-to-channel license table. d(home_i, center(A_k)) <= D_max is not computable, so C0 finding 4 is correct and the plan's spec-2 geographic clause cannot be implemented without new data.
escalations.recommendation: Do not implement geography. Put the trichotomy to Antigravity explicitly, because it is the whole decision: contiguity and the capacity band are properties of the bundle and therefore agent-independent; geography needs data that does not exist; the ONLY agent-specific feasibility predicate in the tree is book overlap S_i(A_j) > 0, which td/stage2_state.py:204-207 already implements as candidacy=True and which tools/staff.py already uses. So the choice is binary: either F_i stays agent-independent and the contracted FEFx is EFX-by-another-name (see E1), or the book-overlap flag is turned ON and FEFx becomes a genuinely different, weaker-per-pair test. If Antigravity wants DOMAIN_economic-theory.md N1's diagnostic to be reachable, overlap must be ON. My recommendation: compute BOTH and report fefx_band_only and fefx_band_overlap side by side with their own n_applicable counts, and never substitute one for the other.
escalations.hazard: Overlap filtering converts a failure into a not-applicable, so turning it on can only reduce the reported failure count. That is a weakening of the audit in the sense plan section 7 item 7 forbids, unless both verdicts are printed together. Also note the perverse reading it licenses: a rep with no book near district j is excused from envying it, which is the opposite of the displacement concern the whole refinement exists to protect. Two further pins if geography is ever added later: the gazetteer vintage (CLAUDE.md trap 22, 468 zips move more than 1 km between the 2020 and 2025 files, 31 zips move on the committed k=18 map) and the tessellation (trap 23, cells are ZCTA polygons while proximity_edges is the Voronoi rook graph, Jaccard 0.411 over 3,704 placed zips). A centroid or drivability test would be a third geometry, and verdicts would not be comparable across runs without both pins recorded.

escalations.question: If the claims reservation makes a slot unstaffable, is adjust-d-down acceptable, or is reject the only honest outcome?
escalations.c0_supported: Reject as the default is correct, and C0's distinction between 'positive surplus on every edge' and 'there exists a complete matching with positive surplus on its matched edges' is exactly right. The clip is not a bargaining-feasibility certificate, as C0 says. But C0's proposed mechanism (clip to eps_floor, then mirror _check_staffable) is unsound, and the repository already contains the correct mechanism.
escalations.counterexample: Verified with the hub interpreter. eps_floor normalized to 1, raw centered surplus g - d = [[0.5, 1.000001], [1.000001, 1.00001]]. Clipping gives costs -log(max(raw,1)) = [[0, -1e-5], [-1e-6, -1e-5]]. linear_sum_assignment returns the diagonal, which uses the clipped edge (0,0), at cost -1e-5, while the anti-diagonal is fully feasible at cost -2e-6. A post-clip staffability check therefore REJECTS even though a complete matching with strictly positive surplus on every matched edge exists. Cause: all clipped edges share one constant cost, so the clip does not separate 'fewest infeasible edges' from 'cheapest total'; two barely-feasible edges can sum above one infeasible edge plus one cheap one.
escalations.correct_mechanism_already_in_tree: td/stage2_state.py:137-161 _match_masked prices forbidden cells at pen = hi + (min(shape)+1)*(hi - lo + 1) over the allowed cost range, then filters them out of the result. That penalty is provably dominant: for a matching using k >= 1 forbidden cells, cost - cost(any all-allowed matching) >= k*(pen - hi) - m*(hi - lo) >= (m+1)*(hi-lo+1) - m*(hi-lo) = (hi-lo) + (m+1) > 0. So _match_masked minimizes the number of forbidden edges lexicographically before anything else, and len(pairs) < n_used_slots is then exactly the Hall shortfall. The same file already raises on that shortfall at lines 211-220 with the comment 'the shortfall is Hall's condition, not an empty column, and only the matching can see it'. On the counterexample above, the mask path returns the feasible anti-diagonal and reports 2 of 2 matched.
escalations.recommendation: Implement the reservation as a mask, not a clip: ok = (g - d_i[:,None]) > tol, run _match_masked on the RAW centered surplus, and take value_centered from the matched pairs' true (unclipped) surpluses, which is what _match_masked already does at line 159. Use len(pairs) == n_used_slots as the bargaining-non-emptiness certificate; equivalently, and as an independent oracle for a test, scipy.sparse.csgraph.maximum_bipartite_matching on ok (verified present in the pinned scipy 1.18.1) detects the same shortfall. Reject when it fails. If a relaxation is ever wanted it must be one of two documented, rank-preserving moves, never a per-rep or per-edge adjustment: (a) a single global scalar haircut t in [0,1] applied to the whole vector d, found by bisection on the largest feasible t, with t emitted as an output key; or (b) a mode downgrade to uniform at the same gamma, which E7 shows is feasible by construction. Per-rep adjustment makes d endogenous to the solve, destroys its reading as an exogenous claim, and makes the 'improved retention' measurement measure nothing the sponsor stated.
hazard: The all-edge guard g_ij - d_i >= 1e-6*d_floor is structurally unsatisfiable in claims mode for any rep whose book is concentrated. Since g_ij = G0_j + (c1-c2)*S_i(A_j) >= G0_j under the contract's own valuation (c1 >= c2 because theta <= 1), the guard's exact form is alpha*S_i(Z) <= min_j[G0_j + (c1-c2)*S_i(A_j)] - gamma*G0_floor, and its sufficient form is alpha*S_i(Z) <= (1-gamma)*G0_floor. On the contract's own toy (c) that sufficient condition fails for 2 of 3 reps, and my check clips 5 of 9 edges at alpha=0.814, gamma=0.60. Clipping is the normal case in claims mode, not an edge case, so compute and log n_reps_guard_violation BEFORE matching rather than discovering it as a clip count.

_check_staffable (td/stage2_state.py:164-170) is a per-column test and is insufficient on its own, by the file's own comment at lines 212-214. C0 section 3 proposes mirroring it; mirror lines 208 AND 211-220.
channel.match raises on any non-positive entry (td/channel.py:298-300), so the centered path cannot reuse it on raw centered surplus; it must go through _match_masked.

If the clip is kept for any reason, one clipped edge contributes log(eps_floor) nats to value_centered. At the contract's own d_floor = 33, eps_floor = 3.3e-5 and log(eps_floor) = -10.3190 nats, which is 160 times the contract's toy delta_centered of +0.064539 nats. So delta_centered comparisons across reservation modes are uninterpretable whenever any edge clips, unless the report also emits n_clipped_matched and the clip penalty separately. Also, every clipped edge has exactly the same cost, so the clip manufactures exact ties and makes reps_swapped fragile across scipy versions.

escalations.question: Plan task 2.4 asserts C_ij remains strictly convex; restate the intended property or drop it.
escalations.c0_supported: Yes. C_ij = -log(max(g_ij - d_i, eps_floor)) is a fixed finite matrix; convexity is a property of a function on a convex domain, not of a matrix, and log(x - d) is strictly concave in x, not convex. C0's diagnosis is right and the implementer must not be asked to write a convexity proof against a matrix.
replacement_properties: P1 domain: g_{i,pi(i)} - d_i > 0 on every matched edge. Certificate: the matching plus the ok mask. This is the only sense in which the log is defined.

P2 bargaining non-emptiness: Hall's condition on the positive-surplus bipartite graph, i.e. a complete matching saturating every used slot exists. Certificate: the matching itself (len(pairs) == n_used_slots), cross-checkable with scipy.sparse.csgraph.maximum_bipartite_matching. This is what plan task 2.4's 'non-emptiness condition' actually names.

P3 exactness: the bipartite assignment polytope is totally unimodular, so the Hungarian optimum equals the LP relaxation optimum and is exact, not heuristic. Test oracle: an LP relaxation solve. Respect the repository traps if used: mip_rel_gap=0.0 for any milp call (trap 12), pin highs-ds with an explicit options dict because scipy 1.18.1's linprog(method='highs') hangs (trap 14), and keep HiGHS out of anything tests/run_all.py imports because HiGHS's thread pool is process-global (trap 18). linear_sum_assignment and csgraph.maximum_bipartite_matching use no HiGHS and are safe inside the runner.

P4 conditioning, which is the property the refinement actually targets: the curvature amplification is |d2/dg2 log(g-d)| / |d2/dg2 log(g)| = (g/(g-d))**2. This reproduces MATH_REVIEW.md:118's 'over 100x' as 177.8x at g=200, g-d=15 (verified). Report min and max of that ratio over matched edges, and report min matched (g-d), rather than any convexity statement.
escalations.correction_c0_missed: Contract section 5 qualifies plan invariant 5 (scale invariance) only for the clip's absolute eps_floor. That is incomplete. With a reservation, scale invariance fails even with no clip active, because sum_i log(kappa*g - d) = n*log(kappa) + sum_i log(g - d/kappa) and d/kappa is not d. Verified numerically at kappa=3.7 on a 3x3 toy: argmax(g,d) and argmax(kappa*g,d) differ, while argmax(kappa*g, kappa*d) equals argmax(g,d). What saves the invariant is that compute_reservation_vector as specified is positively homogeneous of degree 1 in the instance scale: alpha = min(1, region_M/region_T)*(1-epsilon) is degree 0, and S_i(Z) and G0_floor = gamma*min_j G0_j are both degree 1. So the invariant holds only when d is recomputed from the same scaling.
escalations.recommendation: Restate plan task 2.4 as P1-P4 and drop the convexity language. Then close the homogeneity hole in the section 9 API: state_stage2(reservation=ndarray) accepts an absolute vector, so a caller can silently break scale invariance by passing a d built at a different kappa. Either pass the builder rather than the vector, or emit the kappa (median positive ZIP opportunity) the reservation was constructed at into staffing.json next to reservation_mode, and add a test that scaling S, M and G0_floor by kappa scales d by kappa exactly.
escalations.hazard: eps_floor = max(1e-6*d_floor, 1e-12) has an absolute second term that also breaks degree-1 homogeneity. At the descaled scale the repository works at (tau around 180-200 per MATH_REVIEW.md:72) the first term binds, e.g. 3.3e-5 at d_floor=33, far above 1e-12, so the break is latent rather than active. Record the qualification, or drop the absolute term and raise on d_floor == 0 instead, which section 3 already handles as a defined edge case. If the mask recommendation from E4 is adopted, eps_floor disappears from the assignment path entirely and this hazard goes with it.

escalations.question: tools/measure/audits.py and tests/test_audits.py are claimed by unit U6-sel; reconcile ownership before A1.
escalations.c0_supported: The collision is real, and C0 understates it in two directions.
evidence: docs/units/U6-sel.md:5 (status 2026-09-03, A1 track, star-6 lifted) makes the owned files 'tools/measure/audits.py, tests/test_audits.py, docs/MODEL_U6-sel.md, docs/CODEVERIFY_U6-sel.md' and puts 'the 13 x 13 audits on the delivered artifact, EF1 / FEFx-w.r.t.-band / proportionality (N1, N9)' inside the unit's scope, with 'star-5 gates N5 only'. N5 is the core test, not the fairness audits. So A1's deliverable is a strict subset of U6-sel's UNGATED scope, and C0's 'gated on star-5/star-6, not launched' reads as more blocked than the file says.

docs/units/U14-fullprob.md:19-24 (Status: open) owns td/stage2_state.py, td/channels.py, tools/full_plan.py, tests/test_stage2_state.py and tests/test_full_plan_cli.py, plus small edits to td/model.py and td/channel.py. That collides with R1 and R2 as well, and C0 flagged neither.

tools/plan_realise.py is claimed by no unit file (grep over docs/units finds no hit), so M1 and M2 are clean. C0's correction of the re-match home from full_plan.py to plan_realise.py also happens to move that work out of U14-fullprob's owned set, which is a further argument for the correction.

tools/measure/ already follows a one-module-per-unit convention: premium.py belongs to U7-meas with tests/test_measure.py (tests/test_measure.py docstring), alongside frontier.py, district_pieces.py and instance_diff.py.
escalations.recommendation: Route E6 to Luna and the user, not to Antigravity; there is no mathematics in it. Follow the existing per-unit convention and give this job its own module, tools/measure/fefx.py with tests/test_fefx.py, leaving audits.py and test_audits.py to U6-sel. Plan section 8 already requires Luna to record a name mapping before editing an existing target, so record this one. Reconcile R1 and R2 against U14-fullprob the same way before dispatch, since that unit is open on branch worktree-full-problem. The one mathematical constraint on the governance choice: there must be a single shared valuation helper. Two modules computing u_i(A_j) under different conventions (model.utilities masked vs channel.gain_matrix unmasked) will emit contradictory EF1 verdicts on the same delivered map, and nobody will be able to tell which audit is right.
escalations.hazard: tests/run_all.py discovers every test_*.py in tests/, imports it, and runs every callable (tests/run_all.py:4), so a new test file joins the 534-test runner immediately and must pass under .venv alone. It cannot depend on .venv-app (tests/test_app_smoke.py and test_mapfig.py skip there) and, per CLAUDE.md, run_all.py -k cannot select those two because discovery imports every module first. Keep HiGHS out of the new module per trap 18.

escalations.question: 'uniform' reservation mode is undefined in the plan; the contract proposes d_i = d_floor.
escalations.c0_supported: Yes. The plan offers only {none, uniform, claims} and specifies a formula only for claims, so 'a common ambient floor for every rep' is the natural reading, and d_floor = gamma*min_j G0_j is the only common scalar the plan defines. C0 correctly records this as a proposal rather than a claim.
escalations.new_result: Uniform mode is provably clip-free and can never reject. Under the contract's valuation g_ij = G0_j + (c1-c2)*S_i(A_j) with c1 = 1-lam >= c2 = theta*(1-lam), so g_ij >= G0_j >= G0_floor = min_j G0_j. Hence g_ij - d_floor >= (1-gamma)*G0_floor > 0 on EVERY edge for every gamma in [0,1). Verified numerically: G0 = [55, 80, 61], gamma = 0.60 gives min centered surplus 22.0 = (1-0.6)*55 exactly, zero clipped edges, and the spec-1 all-edge guard of 1e-6*d_floor is met with a margin of about 0.667*d_floor. So uniform mode satisfies plan spec 1's guard unconditionally, whereas claims mode violates it routinely (E4).
escalations.recommendation: Adopt d_i = d_floor. Add the above as a tested invariant of R1, not as prose: mode='uniform' implies clipped_edges == 0 and no reject, for any gamma in [0,1) and any non-negative S and M, with gamma == 1 rejected as out of range. Then name uniform-at-the-same-gamma as the documented feasible fallback when claims mode hits a Hall shortfall. That is the honest answer to E4's 'adjust' option: a mode downgrade with a feasibility proof behind it, rather than an ad hoc haircut searched for at runtime.
escalations.hazard: A uniform d is a row-constant shift, so it does not leave the argmax invariant. That is the intended effect (contract finding 8 and toy (d), which I reproduce), but it means uniform mode is not a no-op and must not be described as one. Second, gamma near 1 drives every surplus toward (1-gamma)*G0_floor and the log domain toward the P4 ill-conditioning of E5; require gamma strictly below 1 and report min matched (g-d). Third, 'uniform' at gamma=0 gives d=0 and must reproduce the legacy path bit-for-bit, which is a free regression check on the mode plumbing.

additional_c0_defects_outside_e1_e7: Contract section 13 toy (c) lists d = {r0: 65.571429, r1: 53.357143, r2: 37.071429} and then says 'zero-claim rep d = 33.0'. r2 holds S=5, not 0, and 0.814286*5 + 33.0 = 37.071429 checks out, so the trailing clause describes a hypothetical fourth rep. As written it invites an implementer to treat r2 as the zero-claims case and mis-test the S_i(Z)=0 edge case of section 3. Reword to 'a rep with S_i(Z)=0 would get d = d_floor = 33.0'.

Contract section 3 defines d_floor from G0_j = sum_z [c2*T_z + c_free*S_free(z) + lam*M_z] and then says 'at state grain this is the state-share approximation of G0_j'. td/stage2_state.py:90-103 computes slot sums as (u @ y), i.e. the state-share weighting is applied to the whole utility including the ambient part, so the state-grain G0_j is sum_s y_{s,j} * common(s, B_j) and not the ZIP-grain sum. The two agree only when y is 0/1 (unsplit states). Since R1 runs at state grain and M1 runs at ZIP grain, d_floor differs between the two stages, and the terminal re-match's d is not the Level-0 d. The contract should say which one the migration statistics compare against, or the delta_centered key mixes two different reservations.

Contract section 5's 'Deterministic ties: linear_sum_assignment is deterministic on a fixed matrix and dtype' is true but does not survive the clip. Under the clip every forbidden edge has the identical cost -log(eps_floor), so the tied set can be large and the selected matching among ties is an implementation detail of scipy. The mask path in E4 keeps the ties confined to cells that are filtered out of the result.

Contract section 9 declares PairVerdict.reason to include 'ok' as a reason value while section 2's enum lists only the five not-applicable reasons and says 'every non-evaluated pair carries exactly one reason'. 'ok' is not a not-applicable reason; mixing it into the same field means a consumer cannot count applicable pairs by testing reason != 'ok' without also knowing that convention. learned: LEARNED: Under the contract's valuation convention g_ij = G0_j + (c1-c2)*S_i(A_j) with c1 = 1-lam >= c2 = theta*(1-lam), so g_ij >= G0_j. Two corollaries that decide E4 and E7: uniform mode at d_i = gamma*min_j G0_j has g_ij - d_i >= (1-gamma)*G0_floor > 0 on every edge for any gamma in [0,1), so it never clips and never rejects; claims mode violates the spec-1 all-edge guard whenever alpha*S_i(Z) > (1-gamma)*G0_floor, which is the common case for a concentrated book.

LEARNED: Clipping a log-domain cost at a single constant eps_floor does not make the Hungarian solver avoid infeasible edges. All clipped edges share one cost, so a matching with one clipped edge plus one cheap edge can beat a fully feasible matching of two barely-feasible edges. Verified 2x2 counterexample in this report. td/stage2_state.py:137-161's dominance penalty pen = hi + (m+1)*(hi-lo+1) does have the required separation and minimizes the forbidden-edge count lexicographically.

LEARNED: td/stage2_state.py:211-220 already documents that a per-column staffability check passes when two slots share their only candidate, and that the shortfall is Hall's condition visible only to the matching. Any new feasibility guard must include the len(pairs) == n_slots test, not only _check_staffable.

LEARNED: The only agent-specific feasibility predicate in the tree is book overlap, td/stage2_state.py:204-207 (candidacy=True sets ok = book > 0).
